text_en: For your immortal spirit is in all things.
text_cn: 你那不死不灭的生气在万物之内；

text_en: Therefore you correct little by little those who trespass, and you remind and warn them of the things through which they sin, so that they may be freed from wickedness and put their trust in you, O Lord.
text_cn: 因此，你逐步地惩罚堕落的人，要他们想起所犯的罪恶，藉以警告他们离弃恶事，相信你，上主。

text_en: Those who lived long ago in your holy land
text_cn: 你憎恨你圣地里的古代居民，

text_en: you hated for their detestable practices, their works of sorcery and unholy rites,
text_cn: 因为他们操行巫术和邪恶的祭祀，作出了最可憎恶的事。

text_en: their merciless slaughter of children, and their sacrificial feasting on human flesh and blood. These initiates from the midst of a heathen cult,
text_cn: 这些无情杀害婴儿的人，在这些拜神的歌舞筵会中，吞食人血肉的人，

text_en: these parents who murder helpless lives, you willed to destroy by the hands of our ancestors,
text_cn: 这些杀害无能力自卫生灵的父母，你决意要藉我们先祖的手，将他们消灭，

text_en: so that the land most precious of all to you might receive a worthy colony of the servants of God.
text_cn: 使你以为地上最宝贵的地方，成为天主子民相宜的侨居地。

text_en: But even these you spared, since they were but mortals, and sent wasps as forerunners of your army to destroy them little by little,
text_cn: 但你也拿他们当人对待，先派土蜂作你军队的先锋，逐渐将他们消灭。

text_en: though you were not unable to give the ungodly into the hands of the righteous in battle, or to destroy them at one blow by dread wild animals or your stern word.
text_cn: 这并不是因为你不能用一场战争，使不虔敬者屈服于义人之下；或用凶猛的野兽，或用严厉的言语，一下将他们歼灭；

text_en: But judging them little by little you gave them an opportunity to repent, though you were not unaware that their origin was evil and their wickedness inborn, and that their way of thinking would never change.
text_cn: 而是因你愿逐渐降罚，给他们一个悔改的机会；并不是你不知道他们的种族不良，生来邪恶，永不会改变心意；

text_en: For they were an accursed race from the beginning, and it was not through fear of anyone that you left them unpunished for their sins.
text_cn: 因为他们从起初，就是被诅咒的后裔。 你没有降罚他们的罪行，并非因为你怕谁。

text_en: For who will say, “What have you done? ” or will resist your judgment? Who will accuse you for the destruction of nations that you made? Or who will come before you to plead as an advocate for the unrighteous?
text_cn: 谁敢对你说：你作了什么？谁能反抗你的判断？你消灭了你造的民族，谁敢控告你？又谁敢起来面对着你，为恶人作辩护？

text_en: For neither is there any god besides you, whose care is for all people, to whom you should prove that you have not judged unjustly;
text_cn: 因为，除你以外，别无照顾万物的神，你应向他指明你的审判，并非不公；

text_en: nor can any king or monarch confront you about those whom you have punished.
text_cn: 也没有一个君王或君主，敢为你惩罚的人，对你怒目而视。

text_en: You are righteous and you rule all things righteously, deeming it alien to your power to condemn anyone who does not deserve to be punished.
text_cn: 你是公义的，你必按照公义处理一切；罚不应罚的，你必认为这与你的权威不合。

text_en: For your strength is the source of righteousness, and your sovereignty over all causes you to spare all.
text_cn: 你的权力原是你公义的本源，因为你主宰一切，所以你必能谅解一切。

text_en: For you show your strength when people doubt the completeness of your power, and you rebuke any insolence among those who know it.
text_cn: 为此，如果有人不相信你具有绝对的权威，你就将你的权力显示出来；如果他们知道而仍胆大妄为，你就予以惩罚。

text_en: Although you are sovereign in strength, you judge with mildness, and with great forbearance you govern us; for you have power to act whenever you choose.
text_cn: 你虽掌有大权，但施行审判，却很温和，治理我们，极其宽忍，因为，权能乃属于你，只要你愿意，你就能行使。

text_en: Through such works you have taught your people that the righteous must be kind, and you have filled your children with good hope, because you give repentance for sins.
text_cn: 你这样作，是为教训你的子民，义人必须怜爱众人；并使你的子女满怀希望，因为人在犯罪之后，你常赐予忏悔的机会。

text_en: For if you punished with such great care and indulgence the enemies of your servants and those deserving of death, granting them time and opportunity to give up their wickedness,
text_cn: 你处罚你子女们应处死的敌人，还这样小心温和，给他们时间和机会改恶迁善，

text_en: with what strictness you have judged your children, to whose ancestors you gave oaths and covenants full of good promises!
text_cn: 你审判你的儿子时，岂不更谨慎？因为，你曾与他们的列祖起过誓，立过约，应许他们得福利。

text_en: So while chastening us you scourge our enemies ten thousand times more, so that, when we judge, we may meditate upon your goodness, and when we are judged, we may expect mercy.
text_cn: 你对我们只是惩戒，对我们的仇人却是千百倍的鞭笞（chī）：这是为使我们在审断时，应思念你的仁慈；在受审时，应期望你的哀怜。

text_en: Therefore those who lived unrighteously, in a life of folly, you tormented through their own abominations.
text_cn: 因此，对那生活愚蠢，行为不义的人，你便用他们敬拜的丑恶之物来折磨他们。

text_en: For they went far astray on the paths of error, accepting as gods those animals that even their enemies despised; they were deceived like foolish infants.
text_cn: 他们实在深深地误入了歧途，竟认最丑怪，最下贱的禽兽为神，让自己受骗，竟如无知的孩童。

text_en: Therefore, as though to children who cannot reason, you sent your judgment to mock them.
text_cn: 因此，你对待他们也像无知的孩童，给他们派来的刑罚，也只是戏弄。

text_en: But those who have not heeded the warning of mild rebukes will experience the deserved judgment of God.
text_cn: 但他们并未因此戏弄的责戒而悔改，所以他们要受相称于天主的重罚。

text_en: For when in their suffering they became incensed at those creatures that they had thought to be gods, being punished by means of them, they saw and recognized as the true God the one whom they had before refused to know. Therefore the utmost condemnation came upon them.
text_cn: 埃及人在禽兽的折磨中，有见他们所敬奉为神明的禽兽，成了自己受罚的工具，这才明了，并承认从前所否认的实是真天主； 但他们仍不肯悔改，因此，最后的惩罚终于降在他们身上。
